title: Flat coefficient restriction and normalized derived operations on module diagrams
statement:
Let $J$ be a small category, and let $\mathcal C_U,\mathcal C_V$ be small sites in the module-sheaf universe. Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_U)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_V)$ be a geometric morphism, that is an adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. On each site $T=U,V$ let $a_T:R_T\to S_T$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings. Suppose $S_T$ is flat over $R_T$, meaning $S_T\otimes_{R_T}-$ is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Specify ring isomorphisms $c_R:u^{-1}R_V\simeq R_U$ and $c_S:u^{-1}S_V\simeq S_U$ satisfying $a_Uc_R=c_Su^{-1}a_V$. Put $\mathcal A_{T,R}=\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Mod}(R_T))$ and $\mathcal A_{T,S}=\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Mod}(S_T))$, with module sheaves as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and diagram-site models as in [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Let $r_T$ be termwise restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $L_R,L_S$ be termwise inverse image with the ring action transported by $c_R,c_S$, and $F_R,F_S$ termwise module direct image, whose action uses the adjoint ring map. Use the termwise module adjunctions $L_R\dashv F_R$, $L_S\dashv F_S$. Write $D$ for localization of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; derive exact functors termwise and derive $F_R,F_S$ by K-injective resolutions, where K-injective means every map from an acyclic complex is null-homotopic [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Use the derived adjunctions normalized by [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general].

Restriction $r_T$ is exact and preserves K-injective diagram complexes. There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$b:r_UL_S\xrightarrow{\sim}L_Rr_V,\qquad d:r_VRF_S\xrightarrow{\sim}RF_Rr_U.$$
Here $b$ is the termwise identified inverse image on underlying abelian sheaves. For a K-injective complex $I$ in $\mathcal A_{U,S}$, $r_UI$ computes the restricted object's derived image, and $d_{QI}$ is induced by the underived identity $r_VF_SI=F_Rr_UI$ with its identified ring actions; $Q$ is localization. These comparisons respect adjuncts: for $M\in D(\mathcal A_{V,S})$, $N\in D(\mathcal A_{U,S})$, and $t:L_SM\to N$ with adjunct $t^\sharp:M\to RF_SN$, the adjunct of $r_U(t)b_M^{-1}$ is $d_Nr_V(t^\sharp)$. The comparisons are isomorphisms of derived diagram functors, including all $J$-transition maps.
